avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Increased bleeding risk; ginkgo inhibits platelet aggregation and sulindac increases GI bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use or monitor closely for signs of bleeding

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive antiplatelet effects increase hemorrhage risk
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue high-dose garlic supplements; culinary amounts acceptable

avoid_supplements.name: Ginger (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Enhanced antiplatelet activity combined with NSAID GI irritation
avoid_supplements.action: Limit to culinary amounts; avoid therapeutic supplementation

avoid_supplements.name: Licorice
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Fluid/sodium retention and hypertension risk; increases GI ulceration risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid licorice supplements during sulindac therapy

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have additive anti-inflammatory effects but also increases bleeding risk at high doses
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased GI symptoms or bruising; maintain moderate doses

caution_supplements.name: Feverfew
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet properties may have additive effects
caution_supplements.action: Use cautiously; monitor for bleeding signs

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Anticoagulant properties at high doses may potentiate bleeding risk
caution_supplements.action: Keep supplemental vitamin E below 400 IU daily

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol (regular/heavy consumption)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Significantly increases GI bleeding, ulceration, and hepatotoxicity risk with NSAIDs
avoid_foods.action: Counsel patient to avoid or limit alcohol to minimal amounts; assess daily intake

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: NSAIDs impair sodium excretion; excessive intake increases fluid retention and hypertension risk
caution_foods.action: Recommend moderate sodium restriction; monitor blood pressure

caution_foods.name: Caffeine
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase gastric irritation and GI side effects
caution_foods.action: Moderate caffeine consumption; take sulindac with food to reduce GI upset

monitoring_notes: Monitor renal function, blood pressure, and GI symptoms regularly as sulindac carries NSAID-class risks for GI bleeding, renal impairment, and cardiovascular events. Counsel on signs of bleeding (dark stools, abdominal pain) and report immediately; assess all OTC medication use as many contain NSAIDs.
